title: Full-service wedding floral commissions | Flora Pacifica
copy:
COMMISSIONS
A complete floral world.
For celebrations where flowers are an essential part of the atmosphere, from the closest personal detail to the scale of the room.
FULL-SERVICE FLORAL DESIGN
From a gesture
to an environment.
Floral direction, personal flowers, ceremony installations, reception flowers, and tablescape collaboration are considered together. The final proposal sets out the designs and production needed for your celebration.
Delivery, installation, removal, rentals, custom elements, and travel are scoped explicitly with your venue and planning team.
Our work is best suited to clients who value artistic freedom, seasonal expression, and a cohesive approach to floral design.
INVESTMENT
Individually
considered.
Full-service wedding commissions are individually scoped. Guest count, venue, season, installation complexity, travel, production requirements, and creative direction all shape the investment.
Share your anticipated floral investment with your inquiry. It helps us understand the scale of the celebration and the possibilities within it.
Where does the studio work?
Across Washington and the Pacific Northwest. For celebrations further afield, share the destination so travel and production feasibility can be considered.
Can our planner begin the conversation?
Yes. Include the date, venue, floral priorities, and anticipated investment. The inquiry form welcomes introductions from couples and planning teams.
What happens after an inquiry?
The studio reviews the date, setting, and creative priorities before discussing a consultation. An inquiry does not reserve the date. Booking requirements are confirmed in your agreement.
Can we request specific flowers?
Tell us what you are drawn to. Flower choices depend on season and availability; the overall palette, form, and atmosphere guide the design.

title: Privacy & Your Choices | Flora Pacifica
copy:
YOUR INFORMATION, TREATED THOUGHTFULLY
Privacy & your choices.
This notice describes the private replacement preview. The business must verify its operating practices and approve a complete production notice before public launch.
Inquiries
Submitted name, email, event details, and optional vision are stored in the website’s protected inquiry queue so authorized administrators can review them. No booking is made by submitting a form. The private preview does not send business notifications.
Marketing
The inquiry form does not subscribe you to marketing. Optional website statistics are a separate choice.
Optional website statistics
If you allow statistics, we store limited events such as page paths, selected service category, and successful inquiry interactions. Your name, email, wedding date, message, and other form details are not included in those events. Declining statistics does not disable inquiry or planning features.
Change statistics choices
Essential storage and sign-in
Abuse protection keeps short-lived hashed network identifiers for up to two minutes; it does not store raw network addresses in application tables. This website remembers your statistics choice on your device. Inquiry data is stored on the server. Protected staff spaces use the hosting platform’s supported sign-in. Authentication identifies you; server-side permissions determine which records you can access.
Data requests and retention
The business’s privacy contact, retention schedule, vendor disclosures, and applicable rights must be approved before the replacement is publicly launched. In the private preview, the site owner can delete review records from the protected workspace. Use test details rather than personal information when reviewing.
Third-party links
Instagram, Pinterest, and other linked services have their own privacy practices. External email, CRM, and additional identity providers are not connected in this preview.

title: A calmer start to wedding-flower planning | Flora Pacifica
copy:
← Back to the journal
PLANNING GUIDE
A calmer start to wedding-flower planning
A practical checklist for your first conversation with a florist.
Begin with the moments that matter
Choose the places where flowers will make the most difference to you: the ceremony, your bouquet, shared tables, or a focal installation. You do not need a finished moodboard to start a conversation.
Gather a few useful details
Bring your date or season, venue or location, approximate guest count, floral budget, and any practical access or pickup constraints. A handful of reference images can help communicate feeling without prescribing every stem.
Give your budget a purpose
Decide which floral moments you would prioritize if scope needs to change. A proposal confirms the actual designs, quantities, logistics, and fees.
Leave room for the season
Describe the colors, textures, and feeling you love. Discuss availability and substitutions rather than assuming every flower is available in every month.
Ask about the whole day
Discuss delivery, installation, access windows, rentals, and who handles removal. Confirm responsibilities in your proposal and final plans.

SEASON & PLACE
Flowers that feel at home in Washington
Plan around feeling, texture, and seasonal flexibility.
Let place lead the design
An orchard, a mountain view, a garden, and an urban venue each offer a different starting point. Look at the landscape, light, and spaces where guests will gather.
Plan a palette, not a shopping list
Share favorite tones and textures, then discuss flower choices with your florist. Seasonal flexibility helps a design remain cohesive when individual varieties change.
Prepare for outdoor logistics
Ask your venue about installation access, weather plans, shaded storage, and ceremony-to-reception transitions. Your florist and planner can help translate those constraints into a practical design.
Look at real regional work
Explore our Washington celebrations for garden-inspired, meadow-style, and mountain settings. Each wedding is its own design brief; examples are inspiration, not a promise of identical flowers.

title: What a floral investment makes possible | Flora Pacifica
copy:
← Back to the journal
DESIGN & PRODUCTION
What a floral investment makes possible
The relationship between creative scope, setting, and the work behind an installation.
Start with the experience
An investment begins with priorities: the way a ceremony feels, the intimacy of a table, or the impression of entering a room. Identify the moments that matter before assigning flowers to every surface.
Understand production
A floral installation includes more than flowers. Design development, preparation, transport, labor, access equipment, installation, and removal can all shape the scope. Ask for these responsibilities to be clear in the proposal.
Let the setting inform scale
Guest count, ceiling height, sightlines, table layouts, and access windows influence what is possible. A change of venue or a second event space may require a different production plan.
Work from a shared brief
Bring your anticipated investment and creative priorities to the first conversation. A defined scope gives both client and studio a clear basis for design decisions.
